artifacts.summary: Confirms the root cause (base-mode implement dispatches carry no phase-progress content, so cycle_plan_dispatch_hash() cannot distinguish genuine progress from true repetition), identifies the deploy_pending streak-freeze block and lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh's plan-heading corroboration as ready-made precedents/mechanisms, and recommends an independent-signal freeze (option b) as the required correctness fix layered with an optional always-on phase-progress dispatch section (option a) for transparency, plus the exact Group 37 test-fixture shape (modeled on Group 29) to pin both the fixed and the still-halting case.

memory_candidates.content: orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's deploy_pending streak-freeze (the block immediately above the identical-dispatch halt) is a reusable 'freeze, never suppress' idiom: when an independent per-task signal explains a repeated dispatch-content hash, read the streak counter without incrementing it (never resetting it either), so a pre-existing genuine streak survives the interruption but a second cycle after the explained repeat still accumulates streak normally. Model any new independent-signal exception to a convergence/churn guard on this exact shape rather than re-deriving freeze semantics from scratch.

lib/phase-heading-patterns.sh (PHASE_HEADING_ERE / PHASE_HEADING_DONE_ERE, has_nonconforming_phase_headings) is sourced unconditionally in orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, not hard-mode-gated, even though its only current consumer loop (H1) is hard-mode-only. Any future base-mode feature needing a plan file's own completed/total phase count should reuse this library's grep -cE idiom directly (the same one skill-base.sh's skill_corroborate_phase_counts already uses) rather than re-deriving a phase-counting regex, and must gate on has_nonconforming_phase_headings first per that library's own ordering contract.
